name: Section
summary: A titled region of a page or panel: a heading at a level you set, an optional description and actions, and a body that can collapse.
useWhen: A page or a settings screen splits into titled groups
An inspector or side panel has groups of properties the user opens and closes
A group needs header actions next to its title, such as add or a menu
avoidWhen: Several groups where only one may be open at a time
Switching between views of the same content
A box that needs its own background or border
A hint that shows and hides one short line

title.description: The title. Required. It is the toggle's name when collapsible.

level.description: The heading level of the title, h1 to h6. Required, no default: it follows the page outline and is never guessed. React takes the numbers.

description.description: A line under the title. The toggle points aria-describedby at it.

actions.description: Trailing header actions, outside the toggle.

size.description: sm for panels and inspectors, md for pages.

collapsible.description: The title becomes a toggle that shows and hides the body. With no children there is nothing to disclose, so the header draws alone, with no toggle.

defaultOpen.description: Open state on first render, uncontrolled.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the next open state.

landmark.description: Names the section with its title (aria-labelledby), which makes it a region landmark.

a11y.role: No role of its own: a section element, which is a region landmark only with landmark set. The title is a heading at level. The toggle is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
a11y.focus: A static section is not focusable. A collapsible one puts the toggle in the tab order, then the actions, then the body content.

keys.Tab: Moves to the toggle, then the header actions, then the body
keys.Enter: On the toggle: opens or closes the body
keys.Space: On the toggle: opens or closes the body

a11y.announce: The heading at its level, then the toggle as a button with its expanded state and description. A closed body is hidden from everyone.
notes: The toggle sits inside the heading (the disclosure pattern), so the heading keeps its place in the outline.
Header actions are siblings of the toggle, never inside it: a control inside a control is invalid and unreachable by keyboard.
The chevron points forward when closed and down when open. chevron-forward mirrors in right to left layouts.

en.title: A noun or short noun phrase in sentence case: Billing, Notifications.
en.description: One sentence that says what is inside. No period after a fragment.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics: الفوترة، الإشعارات.
ar.description: White Saudi dialect, one short sentence.

angular.note: Same DOM: the toggle is a dsButton inside the heading. Section.css is used as is.

native.note: The body collapses with the accordion-height preset of the style.

styles.studio: No fill, no radius, a hairline between sections, a bold small title (the inspector section).
styles.desk: The same on the glass of a window. The toggle is a square ghost button with no roll label.
styles.neutral: The same structure, with the Neutral hairline and type scale.
styles.liquid: Content stays solid: a Section is never glass.

mistakes.wrong: An IconButton for add placed inside the toggle
mistakes.right: The actions prop, beside the toggle

mistakes.wrong: Guessing the heading level from nesting
mistakes.right: Set level from the page outline

mistakes.wrong: A collapsible section with nothing inside and a chevron that opens an empty body
mistakes.right: Pass no children: the header draws alone
landmark only for a few regions a user would jump to
